# Lab 2.2: Create Tables & Data Types

## What We Are Going to Do
Create tables three ways (console schema editor, DDL and a JSON schema file) and use the main BigQuery data types.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create a table with the schema editor.** On `lab02` click **⋮ → Create table**:
   - **Source**: Empty table
   - **Table**: `customers_ui`
   - **Schema**: `customer_id INTEGER REQUIRED`, `name STRING`, `signup_date DATE`

   Click **Create table**.

2. **[SQL] Create a table with every main type.**

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab02.type_demo (
  id INT64 NOT NULL,
  price NUMERIC(10, 2),
  big_value BIGNUMERIC,
  ratio FLOAT64,
  is_active BOOL,
  name STRING(100),
  photo BYTES,
  created_at TIMESTAMP,
  local_time DATETIME,
  birthday DATE,
  location GEOGRAPHY,
  attributes JSON,
  valid_period RANGE&lt;DATE&gt;,
  wait_time INTERVAL
);

INSERT INTO lab02.type_demo VALUES (
  1, 199.99, BIGNUMERIC '123456789012345678901234567890.123', 0.75, TRUE, 'Surat Shop',
  b'abc', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), CURRENT_DATETIME('Asia/Kolkata'), DATE '1990-05-01',
  ST_GEOGPOINT(72.8311, 21.1702), JSON '{"tier": "gold", "tags": ["vip"]}',
  RANGE(DATE '2026-01-01', DATE '2026-12-31'), INTERVAL 90 MINUTE
);

SELECT * FROM lab02.type_demo;</span>

3. **[CLI] Create a table from a JSON schema file.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">cat &gt; orders_schema.json &lt;&lt;'EOF'
[
  {"name": "order_id", "type": "INT64", "mode": "REQUIRED"},
  {"name": "customer_id", "type": "INT64"},
  {"name": "amount", "type": "NUMERIC"},
  {"name": "order_ts", "type": "TIMESTAMP", "description": "UTC order time"}
]
EOF
bq mk --table --description="Orders from JSON schema" lab02.orders orders_schema.json
bq show --schema --format=prettyjson lab02.orders</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Compare the three tables.** Open each table's **Schema** tab. Note `REQUIRED` vs `NULLABLE`, and the description on `order_ts`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Three creation methods | Console, DDL and JSON schema all work |
| `NUMERIC(10,2)` | Exact decimal, good for money |
| `GEOGRAPHY` | Point stored as longitude/latitude |
| `RANGE<DATE>` and `INTERVAL` | Native range and duration types |
